title.narrative: Supporting Syrian refugees and vulnerable host communities in the North of Lebanon

description.narrative: Supporting Syrian refugees and vulnerable host communities in Akkar district in North Lebanon (March 2022-February 2024)
Syrian refugees and vulnerable host communities in Akkar region

The Syria Crisis which began in 2011, forced millions of individuals into displacement to seek safety in neighbouring countries (e.g. Lebanon, Turkey, Jordan). Lebanon remains the country hosting the largest number of refugees per capita, with around 1.5 million Syrian refugees who fled their country. Preliminary results of the VASyR 2021 show that 88% of Syrian refugees have expenditure less than the Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (SMEB), unable to meet survival needs of food, health and shelter. In June 2021, 49% of Syrian refugee families were food insecure, and about two-thirds of the families had to limit food portion sizes or reduce the number of meals consumed per day.
In addition, as of late 2019, Lebanon has been facing an unprecedented financial and economic crisis in which the local currency has lost, to date, more than 85% of its value. Over half the population has plunged into poverty due to high inflation and loss of income, and since the beginning of the pandemic both Lebanese and Syrian workers experienced a reduction in wage income of 79%.
Moreover, related to the economic crisis, the Lebanese government started lifting subsidies on fuel (and other essential commodities). Consequently, nation-wide power outages have been more noticeable, affecting the day-to-day operations of individuals and businesses. This development also affects the water authorities in the country. As a result, the 2021 mid-year water sector report showed a significant deterioration in the situation of water supply, with over 71% of people at risk of losing access to water.

The project will aim to support vulnerable households through food parcel distributions and will support the vulnerable area through two interventions, initially by supporting the LRC ambulance station of Wadi Khaled, and by solarizing the public water systems of the North Lebanon Water Establishment in the area so that households can meet their needs in terms of access to safe water.
The ultimate outcomes of the project are envisioned to be the following: 1. Outcome 1 (Livelihoods and basic needs): Communities, especially in disaster and crisis affected areas, restore and strengthen their livelihoods. 2. Outcome 2 (Health): The immediate risks to the health of affected populations are reduced. 3. Outcome 3 (WASH): Sustainable reduction in risk of waterborne and water related diseases in targeted communities in the recovery phase. 4. Outcome 4 (Strategies for Implementation: CEA / Data & Digitalization): The programmatic reach of the Lebanese Red Cross is expanded trough piloting digital Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) models.
